name: Epidermal Moisture Barrier Enhancement
description: Enhances the skin's moisture retention using desert-adapted animal genes, reducing transepidermal water loss by 70–80%. The user requires significantly less water intake — approximately 40% of normal human requirements. The modification also enhances water extraction from food and metabolic water production, allowing the user to survive on minimal water intake that would dehydrate an unmodified human within days. The skin becomes smoother and slightly oilier from the enhanced lipid barrier. In the Shelf, where clean water is expensive and rationed in many buildings, the Camel Mod is a survival modification that reduces dependence on controlled water infrastructure. Gravemoss Biofoundry subsidizes it alongside their other poverty-survival modifications.
source_organism: Camelus dromedarius (dromedary camel), Moloch horridus (thorny devil, moisture harvesting genes)
reversibility: Reversible with lipid barrier normalization treatment
side_effects: Reduced sweating — heat dissipation impaired in hot environments
Urine becomes highly concentrated — kidney stress increases
Reduced tear production — dry eyes in arid conditions
Rare: skin becomes so moisture-retentive that minor cuts seal almost immediately but bleed internally
social_perception: Practical poverty marker, like photosynthetic skin and cellulose digestion. Having the Camel Mod says you can't afford reliable water. Among Tier 1 residents, it's pragmatic. Among higher tiers, it's invisible — they never think about water scarcity.
story_hooks: A Desert Skin community discovers their building's water supply has been deliberately reduced — the landlord knows the residents can survive on less and is diverting the savings
A Dry Runner's enhanced moisture retention makes them uniquely suited to survive in a dehydrated environment that kills everyone else — they're the sole survivor of a sealed-room trap
